title: Foundations: New Wave - The Complete Guide
summary: What New Wave is, where it came from, and how its songs work.
body:
New Wave songs: New wave was punk's poppier sibling: skinny ties, synthesizers, and clever lyrics. Elvis Costello, Blondie, and Talking Heads made nervous energy danceable.

History: 1977–1983: punk's energy plus pop craft plus art-school ideas. MTV made Duran Duran, the Cars, and the Police global stars.

How the songs work: New Wave favors the keys of E, A, G, D. Common forms include Tight verse-chorus, no wasted bars; Dub-inspired breakdowns. Players should master staccato guitar chops first, then reggae-inflected basslines. Guitar-driven; occasional capo.

title: Heart of Glass - New Wave Song Study
summary: Harmonic blueprint and playing guide for Heart of Glass by Blondie (1978).
body:
Heart of Glass — Blondie, 1978. Disco meets new wave; a number one.

HARMONIC BLUEPRINT (study chart, key of G):
G | Em | Am | D

This study chart uses the 'Reggae-rock I–vi–ii–V' progression, the New Wave workhorse, to map how songs like this move. Form: tight verse-chorus, no wasted bars. Listen for ironic, literate lyrics — it is the fingerprint of the style.

TO PLAY IT: set your tempo to the New Wave pocket, voice the chords cleanly, and let ironic, literate lyrics. Guitar-driven; occasional capo. (Song facts: title/artist/year are documented public records; the chart is an original study arrangement.)
